title: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The…
content: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world. These five perceptions, monks, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless.”

title: “Monks, a monk who thinks: ‘Covetousness, unrighteous greed is a defilement of the mind’ and, knowing that, abandons the covetousness, unrighteous greed that is a…
content: “Monks, a monk who thinks: ‘Covetousness, unrighteous greed is a defilement of the mind’ and, knowing that, abandons the covetousness, unrighteous greed that is a defilement of the mind; thinks: ‘Ill-will is a defilement of the mind’ and, knowing that, abandons ill-will, the defilement of the mind; anger … hostility … hypocrisy … spite … envy … stinginess … deceit … fraud … obstinacy … impetuosity … conceit … arrogance … vanity; thinks: ‘Heedlessness is a defilement of the mind’ and, knowing that, abandons heedlessness, the defilement of the mind.”

title: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. This, monks, is not called the ocean…
content: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. This, monks, is not called the ocean in the noble one’s discipline. Here, this world with its devas, Māras, and Brahmās, with its ascetics and brahmins, with its gods and humans, for the most part is submerged in them, tangled like a ball of thread, covered like a tangled skein, become like a tangled grass rope, unable to pass beyond the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, saṃsāra. Monks, there are sounds … odors … tastes … touches … Monks, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. This, monks, is not called the ocean in the noble one’s discipline. Here, this world … for the most part is submerged in them … unable to pass beyond the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, saṃsāra.”

title: When feeling a pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not to be clung to’; he understands: ‘It is not to…
content: When feeling a pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not to be clung to’; he understands: ‘It is not to be delighted in.’ When feeling a painful feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not to be clung to’; he understands: ‘It is not to be delighted in.’ When feeling a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he understands: ‘It is impermanent’; he understands: ‘It is not to be clung to’; he understands: ‘It is not to be delighted in.’ If he feels a pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. If he feels a painful feeling … If he feels a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, he feels it as one who is not bound. When he feels a feeling ending with the body, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling ending with the body.’ When he feels a feeling ending with life, he understands: ‘I feel a feeling ending with life.’ He understands: ‘With the breakup of the body, after death, everything that is felt, in which he no longer delights, will become cool right here.’ Just as, Assaji, an oil lamp burns in dependence on oil and a wick. When the oil and wick of that lamp are exhausted, with no further fuel, the lamp is extinguished. So too, Assaji, a monk, when feeling a feeling ending with the body, understands … when feeling a feeling ending with life, understands … after death, everything that is felt, in which he no longer delights, becomes cool.”

title: Elder Kulla: Kulla went to the charnel ground, Saw a woman abandoned, Thrown away in the cemetery, Food for worms. “Kulla, look at this body…
content:
Elder Kulla:

Kulla went to the charnel ground,
Saw a woman abandoned,
Thrown away in the cemetery,
Food for worms.

“Kulla, look at this body —
Diseased, foul, stinking,
Oozing, seeping,
Delighting fools.”

Having taken up the mirror of Dhamma,
I attained right view.
I contemplated this body —
Empty inside and out.

As it is below, so above,
As above, so below,
As below, so above,
As above, so below.

As by day, so by night,
As by night, so by day,
As before, so after,
As after, so before.

Such a one does not delight
In the five kinds of music.
When one-pointed,
Rightly meditating on the Dhamma.

title: “And how, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives with restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is not defiled by forms cognizable by…
content: “And how, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives with restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is not defiled by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with an undefiled mind, gladness arises. With gladness, rapture arises. With rapture, the body becomes tranquil. With a tranquil body, he experiences ease. For one at ease, the mind becomes concentrated. When the mind is concentrated, phenomena are clearly seen. When phenomena are clearly seen, he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully’ … the ear faculty … the nose faculty … the tongue faculty … the body faculty … If one lives with restraint of the mind faculty, his mind is not defiled by phenomena cognizable by the mind. For one with an undefiled mind, gladness arises … he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully.’ Thus, monks, is dwelling heedfully.”

title: “Furthermore, wanderers, a brahmin says: ‘All sensual pleasures are impermanent, suffering, subject to change.’ That brahmin speaks truth, not falsehood. And by directly knowing the…
content: “Furthermore, wanderers, a brahmin says: ‘All sensual pleasures are impermanent, suffering, subject to change.’ That brahmin speaks truth, not falsehood. And by directly knowing the truth contained therein, he practices disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation regarding sensual pleasures.”

title: (The Blessed One): I am freed From Māra’s trap, Freed from the bonds of sensual pleasures, Both heavenly and human. I am freed From Māra’s…
content:
(The Blessed One):
I am freed
From Māra’s trap,
Freed from the bonds of sensual pleasures,
Both heavenly and human.
I am freed
From Māra’s fetter.
O Death, you are
Defeated.

title: “Monks, one who delights in forms delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in…
content: “Monks, one who delights in forms delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in sounds … in odors … in tastes … in touches … One who delights in phenomena delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who does not delight in forms, monks, does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in sounds … odors … tastes … touches … One who does not delight in phenomena does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

title: - What binds the world? What leads the world? By abandoning what thing Is Nibbāna called? - Delight binds the world, Seeking leads the world,…
content:
- What binds the world?
What leads the world?
By abandoning what thing
Is Nibbāna called?
- Delight binds the world,
Seeking leads the world,
By abandoning craving,
Is Nibbāna called.
